end my remarks by once again thanking mr marias for his is very helpful report. i look forward to hearing the views of the honourable members in the debate.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, i would first like to congratulate the rapporteur on his work. except, of course, for this obsession with german debts, he did a very good job, i think. this is an important report, highlighting the highlights of our activities over the past year. the work of the committee on petitions has improved considerably and become more efficient since the introduction of the new administrative procedure in 2014. it is essential that parliament deal with petitions and give a response to citizens within a reasonable time. to do this, we must concentrate on the petitions that are admissible. another point about the functioning of our committee is the working groups. they should have a clearly defined mandate aimed at facilitating the processing of petitions. the peti committee network is an essential tool which would benefit from greater publicity as it links petitions to legislative work in parliament. we have covered topics that are essential for petitioners this year, and one of those topics is brexit. our committee is a staunch defender of citizens' rights. whether they are british or other europeans, their concerns are legitimate and we must do everything we can to ensure that they are heard. there is also the european citizens' initiative, which must now be used to the full to increase citizens' confidence in the european institutions. cooperation with the european commission and the member states is essential for the handling of petitions, which is why we ask to be informed more and regularly about infringement procedures.
mr president, commissioner, first of all i would like to congratulate the committee on petitions because, from the report, we can all see progress particularly in the quality of the work, because it is not just about quantity. i really believe that petitioning is the way citizens can reveal a problem, usually a problem that they have not been able to solve at the national level. i also think that this committee of ours, the european parliament, is very important and the way petitions are dealt with and, above all, the timing of the communication of the outcome of the petition is important. the citizens must have confidence in the committee on petitions and i believe that the work done by my colleagues was good and complex. the report shows that the number of petitions increased from 2000 to 2016. i also think we need to look at the issues and it can be seen that compared to 2015, when petitions for the environment and justice were at the top, here in 2016, most of the petitions are for the internal market. that is why i recommend that the commission and the member states monitor the way in which the directives governing the internal market are applied, because we all know that this affects the economic environment, but also the lives of citizens.
madam president, commissioner, i am a member of the tran commission and i believe that transport mobility needs to be improved, obviously, taking into account the reduction of emissions, because statistics show that 25% of the emissions in the european union are from transport and 70% from road transport. i am glad that the report has focused on urban transport, where we can have a major contribution to reducing emissions, and i think it is important to switch to alternative fuels first at this level. we know that according to the world health organization, traffic noise is the second most important environmental stressor. so we need a transition to green transport; therefore we need investment in research, in the automotive industry, to have efficient and clean transport. the 2011 white paper on transport makes it very clear that we need a sustainable mobility policy and that we need to rely on a wide range of policy instruments to ensure an effective transition. i appreciate, commissioner, that you mentioned that we need to set realistic targets.
on behalf of the ppe group. madam president, the cambodian supreme court has just made cambodia a one-party state. this decision, unsurprisingly, confirms that justice is in the hands of prime minister hun sen. this is the last step in the dismantling of all political opposition to the regime. the crackdown is not new, it ended with the arrest of kem sokha, accused of plotting with the united states. since his arrest in violation of his parliamentary immunity, the government has launched a propaganda campaign accusing the cambodia national rescue party (cnrp) of being at the center of an anti-government conspiracy. the opposition is not the only victim: media and human rights activists are also victims. how can we expect to organize a free electoral process in july 2018 in such a climate of violation of human rights and the rule of law? i believe that the european union must respond firmly to this authoritarian drift by putting pressure not only on the cambodian government but also on its chinese neighbour, who does not hesitate to encourage this attitude.
madam president, as the banning of the opposition clearly shows, the prime minister and his ruling party are only willing to hold free elections if they are sure that they will win and they do not shy away from deploying anti—democratic practices to secure their rule. sadly, ordering the closure of the main opposition party follows a wider pattern in this regard. independent media outlets have already been reduced to silence and critical ngos have been under attack. the government also expressed its intention to prosecute people who criticise it on social media. unfortunately, these incidents are taking place in the context of a shift away from the west, and the us administration’s diminished interest in human rights. even so, the eu is still the biggest grant donor in cambodia. china has recently increased its aid and investment in the country without human rights strings attached. to reverse this trend, the eu should use all its means to put pressure on the cambodian government to restore the democratic principles from its constitution.
mr president in countries with democratic systems, the lack of political representation of minorities and the resulting conflicts are a constant concern. when a linguistic or ethnically based community is faced with the majority constantly imposing its will, not involving it in decisions that affect the life of the country, or directly discriminating against members of the minority community, then conflict is encoded into the situation. the european union cannot change the political and social systems of all countries, but it could set an example to the world in ensuring human rights and the protection of minorities. unfortunately, this example is not clear today, as the eu institutions do not put pressure on member states for their often deficient policies and practices in the area of minority protection. the report emphasises that minority communities have specific needs and that the rights and full equality of these communities must be promoted in all areas of economic, social, political and cultural life. this finding should also be valid in the union.
mr president, i voted for this report and i have to say that i did not understand the colleagues who did not vote and there were many who did not vote. if we're talking about sexual abuse, if we're talking about this violence against children, i don't think we should have any reservations about making improvements to what's there. now, of course we have directives, we have national regulations, european regulations, but we see that the numbers are frightening. child sexual abuse is on the rise and we need to find new mechanisms, european and national, to ensure on the one hand prevention, education of children, to block these websites - and i am glad that this is included in the report - which promote images of children being sexually abused. and we also need to build shelters and have the infrastructure to get the children out who are enduring this sexual abuse and this violence in the family or in school. so i voted for this report and i hope that there will be a proper application.
mr president i am not pleased that in the last two years a remarkable number of petitions have been received by the committee from romania. in terms of population, it is only surpassed by greece. the almost 100 petitions in one year mean that romanian citizens are aware of their rights related to eu citizenship and the means to exercise them, and this is welcome. however, the very high number of petitions also points to systemic problems in romania, which require the commission's particular attention in certain areas. i do not believe that the rule of law and the guarantee of fundamental rights should be limited to hungary and poland, but that a mechanism covering all member states is needed. the number of petitions shows that in all member states there are cases which can give rise to disputes and which cannot be resolved by the member state authorities. it is certain that if they prefer to select certain countries, romania should be among them.
mr president, i voted for this report. i think we need to know the problems of the citizens. the committee on petitions may take up petitions from european citizens. i'd like to bring up some numbers here. my country is not first. romania is in fourth place, it's not in first place for petitions, but one thing again relevant has dropped. and perhaps most relevant is to look at what sector the petitions are coming from. first of all, as a field of activity, in 2016 the petitions were related to how the internal market works and not to the environment and not to justice and not to human rights. so i think that we, the european parliament, the commission, the national authorities, have to see what the citizens are complaining about in relation to the functioning of the internal market and demand that a fair market is put in place. finally, citizens' rights are also linked to the functioning of the internal market and i believe that this report brings improvements and we, meps, must say in our countries that there is this lever through which the citizen can complain about a problem that has not been solved in his country.
mr president, as a member of the tran committee and of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, i voted in favour of this report. there are a lot of things that bring improvement. we all know that transport affects the competitiveness of our economies in our countries and in the internal market. at the same time, i was glad that the report focused on urban transport and i believe - and i said in the plenary - that we need to start there, with urban transport, to move from a petrol-fuelled to electric cars and vehicles. i also welcome the commissioner's position and the report also sets out what was included in the 2011 white paper on the transition to green transport: to take into account the impact on small and medium-sized enterprises, to invest in technology and research, to have car fleets and the necessary infrastructure for electricity supply and thus to achieve a competitive and clean economy.
